title: One random order, many arrivals
hook: The first assignment may consume a later arrival’s only neighbour.

knows: Compare numbers; read a short array, string, tree or graph as drawn.
Offline optimum versus online decisions; cost and approximation ratio.
doesNotKnow: Match online arrivals to the highest-ranked available neighbour under one fixed random ranking.

misconception: Choosing the first listed available neighbour has the same behaviour as a shared random ranking.
objective: Match online arrivals to the highest-ranked available neighbour under one fixed random ranking.

claims.text: One fixed offline ranking breaks choices throughout the run. Giving A the first-ranked available neighbour can consume B’s only option. The opposite fixed ranking changes this tiny outcome; the randomized algorithm’s guarantee concerns random rankings, not either single run.
